title: Spiced Pumpkin Pancakes with Toasted Pecans
changes_from_base: The pumpkin purée is first cooked down with sugar and spices, milk and oil replace the buttermilk and butter, and each pancake is scattered with toasted pecans before flipping.
summary: Warm, spiced pumpkin pancakes studded with toasted pecans, gently sweet and fragrant with autumn spices.
equipment: nonstick frying pan (30 cm) or griddle

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
neutral oil or melted butter, plus a little oil for the pan

steps.title: Mix dry
steps.text: Whisk 255 g plain flour and 3½ tsp baking powder.

steps.title: Cook pumpkin
steps.text: Cook 425 g tin unsweetened pumpkin purée, 50 g caster sugar, 1 tsp ground cinnamon, a scant ½ tsp fine salt and ¼ tsp ground nutmeg over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thick, glossy and reduced to about 240 ml (6-8 min).

steps.title: Add liquid
steps.text: Off the heat whisk in 60 ml vegetable oil (or melted butter), 180 ml whole milk (room temperature) and ¼ tsp vanilla (optional); cool 5 min, then whisk in 2 large eggs (room temperature).

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Pour into the flour and stir until just combined (lumpy); rest 10-15 min.

steps.title: Heat pan
steps.text: Heat 1 tsp oil in a 30 cm non-stick or cast-iron frying pan over medium-low heat until shimmering (about 5 min) and wipe out the excess with kitchen paper. Test with 1 tbsp batter (pale golden after 1 min).

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Spoon 3 portions of 60 ml, spread each to 10 cm and sprinkle each with about 1 tbsp toasted finely chopped pecans; cook until bubbles break, edges are set and base is golden (2-4 min). Flip and cook 1-3 min more. Keep warm on a rack in a 93 °C oven if you like; repeat, adding oil as needed.

tips: Reduce the pumpkin purée over the heat to concentrate its flavour and remove excess moisture, keeping the pancakes fluffy rather than dense.
Toast the pecans lightly before chopping to bring out their nuttiness and add crunch.
A gentle medium-low heat prevents the spices and pecans burning before the pancake cooks through.
storage: Best served fresh and warm. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
